segments.title: Cold Open: Pepito Sign-On
segments.notes: Pepito delivers the station identification as 'Papita the dog' before the broadcast begins.

segments.title: Opening Monologue: Mass Staff Layoffs & Hype Train
segments.notes: Case Blackwell returns from illness to announce half the staff (Jeff Ripple, Rick, Tyler, Sammy, Salazar, Garf) have been 'doged' and quit; Pepito is incapacitated on Jolt Cola; Hype Train dominates the broadcast with a 25-minute freestyle rap over subscriber alerts.

segments.title: International Desk: Dmitry on Trump-Macron Ukraine Talks
segments.notes: New correspondent Dmitry (Russian expat with purple sunglasses and beard) provides a goon-centric analysis of Trump and Macron's meeting, framing geopolitics as a 'nuclear meat-slapping contest' and predicting Ukraine will be left 'gooning in the cold'.

segments.title: Debate: Who Should Be Laid Off?
segments.notes: Crum owes the Rock-afire gorilla $170,000; Munch forces a new wager where Crum must argue for his own firing to win $5,000, while Munch argues Crum should stay — both sides devolve into meta pleas for termination.

segments.title: React Segment: Peter Gibbon Returns from the Walls
segments.notes: Peter Gibbon emerges from the crawlspace to co-host a react segment featuring viral clips (Jackie Chan stunts, pickup lines, Guitar Center beat-making, driving safety), punctuated by Peter's tantric claims and Case's mounting discomfort.

segments.title: News Desk: Liliana on Elon Musk's Botched Penis Surgery
segments.notes: Liliana reads an Azalea Banks tweet alleging Elon Musk's failed penile implant, speculating on 'weeping willow' anatomy and a Mephisto-style deal for wealth; segment ends with a 'soggy bottom boy' penis taxonomy.

segments.title: How To with Jeb's Dad (feat. Crum)
segments.notes: Jeb Nogget is absent after a DIY face-lift; his deceased father (trapped in a wooden board) hosts with Crum filling in, watching sausage-making and tantric yoga videos while bickering about the afterlife.

segments.title: News Desk: Kyle's Rapid-Fire Headlines
segments.notes: New correspondent Kyle (clinically dead eyes, former face tattoos, oxy history) delivers a chaotic rundown including Technicolor bankruptcy, Trump vs. lesbian judge, Elon's 'Harry Balls' rename, JoAnn Fabrics closure, Stephen King on Dark Tower, Island Boys arrest, Lester Holt stepping down, and a Canadian thumbs-up emoji contract case.

segments.title: Sign-Off & Raid
segments.notes: Case closes the broadcast, mentions feeding Kendelle, teases a potential call-in show, and raids Ricky Peacock.

characters.name: Case Blackwell
characters.notes: Anchors the return broadcast while managing a gutted staff roster and a parade of replacement correspondents.

characters.name: Pepito
characters.notes: executive producer. Incapacitated by vintage Jolt Cola consumption, leaving production duties to Case's cousin Jake Whitehole.

characters.name: Hype Train
characters.notes: hype correspondent. Commandeers the opening block with a 25-minute freestyle rap over sub alerts, declaring dominance over the depleted crew.

characters.name: Munch (Ralph Munchcut)
characters.notes: debate analyst. Presides over the layoff debate, goading Crum into arguing for his own termination while claiming immortality.

characters.name: Crum (Leonard Crum)
characters.notes: debate analyst. Begs viewers to vote for his firing to win $5,000 toward his $170,000 gorilla debt, then fills in for Jeb's dad on How To.

characters.name: Peter Gibbon
characters.notes: news stowaway. Emerges from the walls to co-host Amongst the Web, claiming he was 'doged' but returned for spoiled mannies.

characters.name: Liliana
characters.notes: desk partner. Co-anchors the Elon Musk penis surgery story, describing her womb as a 'hostile place' for a Musk child.

characters.name: Jeb's Dad
characters.notes: wood-trapped spirit. Hosts How To with Jeb while his son recovers from facial surgery, bickering with Crum from inside a wooden board.

characters.name: Dmitry
characters.notes: international correspondent. One-off Russian expat correspondent who frames Ukraine geopolitics through 'goon squad' survival theory.

characters.name: Kyle
characters.notes: field correspondent. Debut correspondent with clinically dead eyes and a history of face tattoos and oxy use; delivers a surreal rapid-fire news rundown.

characters.name: Jake Whitehole
characters.notes: production assistant. Case's cousin, pressed into button-pushing duty while Pepito is incapacitated.

storylines.beat: [49:16] Crum's debt to the Rock-afire gorilla stands at $170,000; Munch imposes a new wager where Crum must argue for his own firing to earn $5,000 per win.
[02:18:02] Case references the Beyblade Tournament as 'quietly sunsetted like CTDS and Colcast,' suggesting the community pledge remains unfulfilled.

lore_notes.fact: Crum pays approximately $1,000 per week in interest to the Rock-afire gorilla to keep the $170,000 debt from growing.
Crum is entangled in legal disputes from his marriage in Rennerton, where deceased citizens retain the ability to hire lawyers from billboards.
Jeb Nogget underwent a DIY face-lift/jaw surgery that left him unrecognizable; his father states Jeb is recovering from 'facial paralysis.'
Salazar (tentacled correspondent) was deported when the transatlantic swimming route was closed.
Justin Powers (unspecified role) is mentioned as unlikely to return.
Kyle has 'dead eye syndrome' — a clinically dead section of his face — and spent 12 years removing full face tattoos after repeated oxy-related traffic stops.
Liliana describes her womb as radiating 'slightly murderous' energy, comparing a hypothetical Musk pregnancy to 'sending a search party into Chernobyl.'
Case's cousin Jake Whitehole is now on payroll as a production assistant.

episode_summary: Case Blackwell returns from a week-long illness to find half the BIN staff 'doged' into resignation, leaving Pepito incapacitated on Jolt Cola and production in the hands of Case's cousin Jake. The broadcast cycles through a gauntlet of replacement correspondents — Dmitry, Peter Gibbon, Liliana, Jeb's undead father, Crum, and debutant Kyle — covering Trump-Macron talks, Elon Musk's alleged botched penile implant, a sausage-making tutorial, and a Canadian lawsuit over thumbs-up emoji contracts, all while Crum's $170,000 gorilla debt looms over a forced layoff debate.
